{"edit_description":"Create a brand-new, fully self-contained single-file HTML page (no external assets, no libraries, no WebGL — Canvas 2D only) implementing a realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating cube. File layout: <!DOCTYPE html>, <meta charset="utf-8">, <title>Gouraud-Shaded Cube — Canvas 2D</title>, full-viewport dark background, a <canvas id="c">, a small monospace HUD overlay (absolute positioned divs) for title, FPS, status (PAUSED/WIREFRAME indicators) and key hints. All JavaScript inline in one <script> at the end. Clean, commented, English code.

Functional spec:

1. GEOMETRY: 8 cube vertices at (±1, ±1, ±1). 6 quad faces, each split into 2 triangles (12 triangles). Define faces with consistent counter-clockwise winding when viewed from outside (so backface culling by signed screen-space area works). Give each face its own distinct base hue.

2. MATRIX PIPELINE: implement small mat3/mat-vector helpers. Rotation matrices Rx, Ry, Rz built from time-varying angles (each axis spins at a different speed, e.g. 0.6, 0.9, 0.35 rad/s). Compose M = Rz * Ry * Rx (or similar) and transform every vertex each frame.

3. PER-VERTEX LIGHTING (Lambert): per-vertex normal = the rotated, normalized vertex position (normalize(v.x, v.y, v.z)) so lighting interpolates smoothly across faces — this is what makes Gouraud gradients visible on the cube. Moving light: L = normalize( (cos(t)*4, sin(t*0.7)*3, sin(t)*4 + 3) ) orbiting the cube. intensity = ambient + kd * max(0, N·L). Compute a final r,g,b (floats 0..255) per triangle vertex from face base color × intensity.

4. PERSPECTIVE PROJECTION: camera distance 4 along +z. sx = x * f / (z + 4), sy = -y * f / (z + 4), f = min(w, h) * 0.85, plus screen center offset (w/2, h/2).

5. BACKFACE CULLING: signed area of the 3 projected 2D vertices (cross product); skip triangles whose winding shows back-facing (sign consistent with the y-flip and CCW faces). Skip degenerate (near-zero area) triangles.

6. GOURAUD RASTERIZER (the core): a true software per-pixel rasterizer writing into an ImageData buffer. Allocate one ImageData per canvas resize; per frame clear it (or use a Uint32Array view for fast fill), then for each culled front-facing triangle rasterize by scanline/barycentric incremental interpolation: compute bounding box, per-pixel barycentric coordinates or edge walking, linearly interpolate the three vertex r,g,b values across the interior in screen space, clamp 0..255, write pixels. NO flat fillStyle fills — interpolated per-pixel colors are mandatory (that is Gouraud shading). Use a Uint32Array view over ImageData.data.buffer with packed ABGR little-endian pixels for speed. Clamp x,y to canvas bounds. putImageData once per frame.

7. WIREFRAME TOGGLE (key 'W'): switch to wireframe rendering — stroke triangle edges using canvas paths, colored by the lit vertex colors (per-edge linear gradients between the two projected vertices' colors, or the average lit color — gradients preferred for consistency). Backface culling still applies so back edges are hidden. Toggle back to shaded with W again.

8. PAUSE (key 'P'): freeze the rotation angles and the light motion (stop advancing time used for animation); keep the render loop + FPS counter + key handling alive so W still works while paused. Show 'PAUSED' in the HUD when active.

9. FPS DISPLAY: exponential moving average of frame deltas; render as integer FPS in the HUD every frame (or throttled to ~4 Hz updates of the text). Use performance.now() deltas, guard against zero dt.

10. RESIZE: window resize listener recreates canvas size + ImageData buffer; canvas fills the window.

11. Polish: background #0b0e14, subtle HUD styling (semi-transparent), bottom-left hint line "W — wireframe · P — pause". requestAnimationFrame main loop. No external dependencies whatsoever; everything inline.","path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_zai-glm-5.3_01.html"}
